claim: Gao-Han-Li-Zhou (JFE 2018): on SPY 1993-2013, first half-hour return (measured from previous close, so it includes the overnight gap) predicts last half-hour return; stronger on volatile, high-volume, recession and macro-news days; present in ten other ETFs.
quote: the first half-hour return on the market as measured from the previous day’s market close predicts the last half-hour return.
title: Market intraday momentum (JFE abstract, EconPapers)

claim: Working-paper version of Gao et al on SPY Jan 1999-Dec 2012: holding SPY in last half-hour only after positive first half-hour gave 6.3% gross annualised vs -0.5% always-hold; frictions ignored (CXO summary, secondary).
quote: Holding SPY (cash) during the last half-hour when the first half-hour return is positive (negative) generates a gross annualized return of 6.3%, compared to -0.5% for holding SPY during all last half-hours.
title: First and Last Half Hours of Trading Linked? (CXO Advisory)

claim: Independent SPY check Aug 2012-May 2014 (441 days): correlation first vs last half-hour 0.12, R-squared 0.014; effect driven by extreme first half-hour returns, and late-day moves too small to survive frictions (CXO).
quote: The Pearson correlation for the relationship is 0.12 and the R-squared statistic 0.014, indicating that first half-hour return explains 1% to 2% of the variation in last half-hour return.
title: First and Last Half Hours of Trading Linked? (CXO Advisory)

claim: Rosa (JFM 2022): for the variant using overnight return to predict last half-hour, predictability disappears out of sample; thresholded strategy beats always-on.
quote: The predictability disappears in the out‐of‐sample period.
title: Understanding intraday momentum strategies (Rosa, JFM)

claim: Baltussen et al (JFE 2021): over 60 futures 1974-2020, return from prior close to last 30 minutes positively predicts last-30-minute return everywhere; linked to gamma hedging demand; reverts over next days.
quote: we find strong market intraday momentum everywhere.
title: Hedging demand and market intraday momentum (JFE abstract)

claim: Zarattini-Barbon-Aziz (2024): 5-minute ORB on top-20 'Stocks in Play' (7,000+ US stocks, 2016-2023) net total performance over 1,600%, Sharpe 2.81, alpha 36% after costs; S&P passive 198% (self-published working paper).
quote: A portfolio that consisted of the top 20 Stocks in Play achieved a total net performance of over 1,600%, with a Sharpe ratio of 2.81, and an annualized alpha of 36%.
title: A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market (Concretum/St Gallen WP)

claim: Zarattini-Aziz QQQ 5-min ORB: 33.2% vs 14.9% CAGR, Jan 2016-Feb 2023, 1,795 trades; per CXO assumed zero slippage, no bid-ask spread, 4x leverage, $0.0005/share commission.
quote: A 5-minute opening range breakout day-trading strategy on QQQ (long/short after first 5 minutes; 1% risk per trade; daily exit) outperformed buy-and-hold QQQ (33.2% vs 14.9% CAGR; Jan 2016–Feb 2023; 1,795 trades; zero slippage assumed).
title: Day Trading with an Opening Range Breakout Strategy (CXO)

claim: Independent trader replication of Zarattini-Aziz ORB on NQ, SPX, Dow, DAX, FTSE CFDs 2015-2026 (self-reported blog): out-of-sample 2021-2026 gives +0.06 R on NQ at best with spread and slippage; first-candle direction beats random direction by +0.10 to +0.13 R in NQ, DAX, FTSE (gross).
quote: The out-of-sample years 2021 to 2026 give +0.06 R on NQ at best; futures with commission only were not tested.
title: The opening-range breakout paper, replicated on five indices: gross reproduced, net zero (MQL5 blog)

claim: Same replication concludes first 5-minute candle direction carries a small real directional edge, about the size of the CFD spread.
quote: The colour of the first 5-minute candle carries a small, real directional edge against a random-direction benchmark, present in four of five indices and still there out of sample.
title: The opening-range breakout paper, replicated on five indices (MQL5 blog)

claim: Lou-Polk-Skouras (JFE 2019): firm-level overnight and intraday returns each continue and cross-period reverse for years; momentum/reversal strategy profits earned entirely overnight or entirely intraday, usually with opposite signs.
quote: profits are either earned entirely overnight (for reversal and a variety of momentum strategies) or entirely intraday, typically with profits of opposite signs across these components.
title: A tug of war: Overnight versus intraday expected returns (JFE abstract)

claim: Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka (JF 2010): cross-section of stock returns shows continuation at half-hour lags that are multiples of a trading day, lasting at least 40 days; short-term reversal driven by liquidity imbalances lasting under an hour.
quote: We find a striking pattern of return continuation at half‐hour intervals that are exact multiples of a trading day, and this effect lasts for at least 40 trading days.
title: Intraday patterns in the cross-section of stock returns (JF abstract)

claim: Glasserman et al (2025, arXiv): over 30 years nearly all US stock gains were earned overnight while average intraday returns were negative or flat; news topics explain a large part.
quote: Over the past 30 years, nearly all the gains in the U.S. stock market have been earned overnight, while average intraday returns have been negative or flat.
title: Does Overnight News Explain Overnight Returns? (arXiv 2507.04481)
